answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a bond locked in a public ledger and slash it when a randomly selected, independently verified task reveals duplicate control or fabricated work. A single operator can still create many identities, but each must post capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing every bonded stake; splitting into aliases does not multiply the operator's funds. This creates an inlet to a lagoon of trusted activity without pretending to bar the ocean of cheap, unverified identities.
